name: Sivagrayogin
dates_notes: Usually assigned to sixteenth-century South India, but the available biographical notices and manuscript evidence do not justify a more precise date range here.
sub_school: Sanskrit and Tamil Śaiva Siddhānta — technical exposition
core_thesis: Śivāgrayogin is a South Indian Śaiva Siddhānta author who composed Sanskrit and Tamil expositions of the Meykaṇṭār tradition. His *Śaivaparibhāṣā* organizes its technical vocabulary and categories, while his Sanskrit commentary on *Śivajñānabodham* relates the Tamil foundational work to wider āgamic materials. His importance lies in this conceptual and bilingual mediation: he supplies later scholastic readers with a technical map of Siddhānta rather than founding a separate system.

engaged_works.title: Saiva-paribhasa
engaged_works.ascription_notes: The text is securely transmitted under Śivāgrayogin's name and has been edited and translated.
engaged_works.summary: A Sanskrit manual in five sections that defines and orders key Śaiva Siddhānta technical terms and categories. A modern edition and English translation exist; no verified local primary-text witness has been linked here.

engaged_works.title: Sivajnana-bodha-bhasya
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Standardly transmitted as Śivāgrayogin's extensive Sanskrit commentary on Meykaṇṭār's *Śivajñānabodham*.
engaged_works.summary: An extensive Sanskrit commentary on Meykaṇṭār's Tamil *Śivajñānabodham*. It is significant for bringing āgamic parallels into the interpretation of the Meykaṇṭār school; passage-level claims are deferred until a primary text is acquired and checked.
